chunks: Hadith 956 — Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say, when he had finished at noontime:

"O Allah, I seek nearness to You through Your munificence and Your generosity, and I seek nearness to You through Muḥammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, and I seek nearness to You through Your near angels and Your sent prophets. And through You, O Allah—Yours is independence from me, and mine is need toward You. You are the Self-Sufficient, and I am the needy one toward You. Overlook my slip, conceal my sins from me, fulfill today my need, and do not punish me for the ugliness of what You know from me; rather, Your pardon encompasses me, and Your generosity."

Then he would fall in sajdah and say: "O Possessor of taqwa and O Possessor of forgiveness, O Benign, O Merciful, You are more benign toward me than my father, my mother, and all creatures. Turn me back with the fulfillment of my need, my supplication answered, my voice shown mercy. You have indeed removed the various kinds of affliction from me."

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the noontime period after the sun passes the meridian
key_terms.الْغَنِيُّ: the One free of all need, absolutely self-sufficient
key_terms.الْفَقِيرُ: the one in need and dependence upon Allah
key_terms.الْمُقَرَّبِينَ: those brought near to Allah, here referring to the near angels
key_terms.بِجُودِكَ: through Your munificence and open-handed generosity

ai.seo_question: What du'a did Imam Ali عليه السلام recite after the noontime prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith records a supplication of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام after the noontime prayer, expressing nearness to Allah through His generosity and through Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the angels, and the prophets. It centers on poverty before Allah, seeking pardon, concealment of sins, fulfillment of needs, and mercy in sajdah.
